Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Secy.Home And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Brijesh Kumar,Arvind Kumar,Pradeep Kumar Shukla,Prithvish Mishr
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,G.A.,Suneel Kumar Maurya,Sunilkumar Maurya Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.
The name of Shri Suneel Kumar Maurya, Advocate is printed in the cause list as learned counsel for the opposite party no.2.
However, he is not present nor any request has been made on his behalf to adjourn the case.

Heard Shri Pradeep Kumar Shukla, learned counsel for the accused/applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
This bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant- Anoop Kumar for grant of bail, in Case Crime No. 308 of 2022, under Sections 376,323, 506,147 IPC & Section 3/4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, Police Station Mailani, District Kheri, during trial.
Learned counsel for the accused-applicant while pressing the bail application submits that the accused-applicant has falsely been implicated in the instant case and he has not committed any Anoop Kumar vs State Of U.P. sentences.text: It is further submitted that the allegations of making sexual relations on the pretext of false promise of marriage levelled against the applicant in the FIR as well as in the statement of the prosecutrix recorded U/s 161 & 164 CrPC, are patently false and absurd and could not be believed.

It is further submitted that the FIR of this case has been lodged by moving an application U/s 156(3)
CrPC which has been drafted on the advice of a legal professional and accusations mentioned therein have been made in order to harass the applicant for the purpose of keeping him in jail for a long time.
It is also submitted that even if the statement of the prosecutrix recorded U/s 161 & 164 CrPC is taken on its merits, it would reveal that she was having an affair with the applicant and the sexual relations have been made by them with consent.
It is also submitted that no obscene video, etc. has been recovered during the course of investigation.
The age of the prosecutrix, as per educational credentials, which are not conclusive, is 17 years and 11 months.

So even if the case of the prosecution is believed, the prosecutrix at relevant point of time was having sufficient intellect to understand her welfare and as she was a consenting party, no offence in fact has been committed by the applicant.
It is further submitted that the applicant is in jail in this case since 26.8.2022 and he is not having any criminal antecedents.
Charge sheet in the matter has already been filed.
Having regard to the pendency before the trial court, the trial is not going to conclude in the near future.
There is no apprehension that the accused-applicant after release on bail, may flee from the process of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.
Learned A.G.A., on the other hand submits that having manner on which the offence has been committed the applicant is not entitled for any relief.
Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is evident that the FIR of this case has been lodged after orders of the magistrate passed U/s 156 (3) CrPC.
The prosecutrix in her statement U/s 161 & 164 CrPC, has admitted that she was having an affair with the applicant.
The factum of making sexual relations on the basis of the false promise of marriage has been denied by the applicant.

Whether the sexual activity between the prosecutrix and the applicant was a result of false promise of marriage, may only be determined after considering the evidence of the prosecution led before the trial court, during the course of trial.
The medical report of the prosecutrix is not showing any abnormality.

She, at the date and time of the alleged incident,
was about 17 years and 11 months as per her educational certificate.
The applicant is jail in this case since 26.8.2022 without any criminal history.
Charge sheet in the matter has already been filed.
His presence could be secured before the trial court by placing any adequate conditions.

Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion Anoop Kumar vs State Of U.P. sentences.text: on the merits and demerits of the case, I am of the considered view that applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant- Anoop Kumar involved in the aforesaid case be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(ii) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
Observations made herein-above are only for the purpose of disposal of bail application and the same shall not have any bearing on the trial of the case.
